Hi Liam — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we have a single thread for the POC kickoff.

What we covered (short):
- Primary objective: semantic search + summarization for customer support transcripts (median doc length ~650 tokens, peak sessions with 3 concurrent queries).
- Key constraints: p95 latency target <= 300ms for single-query UI, budget target ~ $Xk/month for inference (we'll refine after workload profile).

Redwood-recommended model shortlist (tradeoff notes included):
1) rwd-verified/gptx-slim-7b (int8) — Best quality-per-cost for <300 token responses; throughput: 180 TPS observed in our hosted baseline; latency percentiles (hosted profile): p50=85ms, p95=290ms, p99=470ms. Good default for early evals where quality matters.
2) openclaw-70b-8bit — Highest quality on long summaries; throughput: 48 TPS; p50=210ms, p95=480ms, p99=890ms. Requires Dedicated capacity for consistent p95.
3) rwd-quant-13b-q4f16 — Lowest token cost with competitive quality for retrieval-augmented prompts; throughput: 240 TPS; p50=70ms, p95=260ms, p99=420ms. Strong candidate if you prioritize cost and latency.

Attached are three artifacts: a) Redwood-verified performance profiles (pdf) showing how TPS and latency were measured, b) a prompt-pack tailored to your call transcripts (zip), and c) a small benchmark sample CSV (first 200 calls) so you can reproduce locally.

Files + what to check quickly:
- Redwood perf profiles: look at the sequence-length distribution section — we simulated your 650-token median.
- Prompt pack: examples labeled SUMMARIZE_SHORT, ANSWER_CONCISE, RERANK_SNIPPET. Use SUMMARIZE_SHORT first.
- CSV: run the provided harness with our instructions (link below) to compare latency on your infra.

Quick answers to things you asked on the call:
- Can we hit p95 <= 250ms? Possibly, but depends on deployment. On-hosted we see p95 around 260–320ms for the 13B quant profile; Dedicated with pinned GPUs + optimized kernel selection regularly gets p95 < 250ms for the rwd-quant-13b profile.
- Token cost: estimate attached in the perf profiles page (section 3).

Proposed mutual action items (suggested cadence):
1) Nimblesurf: confirm sample dataset access and preferred security controls (S3 presigned or sharepoint link) — due by Wed 3/3.
2) Redwood: provision evaluation runner and provide a short Cloud/SSH guide for your infra — target 2 business days after dataset receipt.
3) Technical deep-dive: 60-minute session with your infra + eng team to align on latency SLOs and batching policy — propose Tue 3/2 or Wed 3/3.
4) Decide POC target: "latency-first" or "quality-first" (we recommend latency-first to validate UX).

If that looks right, I'll queue a dedicated trial quote and send the perf profiles link to your procurement contact.

Thanks,
Irene

Liam — quick technical notes to help with the PM question. Short version: getting from p95=260ms -> <=250ms is doable but not guaranteed on hosted for the full traffic profile; steps we recommend if you need deterministic p95: 
- Dedicated capacity: pin a GPU worker fleet (no noisy neighbors) and use our low-latency kernel path — typical improvement of 10–20% on p95.
- Quantization + token cap: rwd-quant-13b-q4f16 with max_output_tokens=200 reduces tail latency; combined with continuous-KV cache for session reuse gives the best improvement.
- Batch sizing: set max_batch_ms=10 and prefer many small batches (continuous batching) for UI workloads.

For the 70B: memory footprint depends on quantization. Openclaw-70b-8bit uses ~60GB VRAM in our baseline; we support CPU fallback offload for KV cache but performance drops significantly. If you plan mixed infra, Dedicated with a single high-memory GPU (A100 80GB or equivalent) is recommended.

SOW/trial quote: Irene/Tessa — we can draft a 6-week POC SOW (scope: dataset ingest, 2-week hosted eval, 4-week dedicated trial optional) and include a pricing appendix for hosted vs dedicated. I can assemble numbers once procurement confirms target monthly tokens.

If you want, I can run a short microbenchmark (using your sample CSV) on our Dedicated lab and share p50/p95/p99 curves tomorrow.

— Dev
